description: Daily Quiz sets shown on /quiz, keyed by date (YYYY-MM-DD, India time). Each set has 5 MCQs. New sets are added only after Kenil approves them in chat. The first set below is a sample drawn from existing module quiz items.

questions.stem: A 4-year-old has septic shock in a hospital with a PICU. How should the first-hour fluid be given?
options: 10–20 mL/kg boluses, reassessing after each, up to 40–60 mL/kg in the first hour
No fluid; start adrenaline straight away
questions.explanation: Where intensive care is available, the 2020 SSC paediatric guideline suggests up to 40–60 mL/kg as 10–20 mL/kg boluses. Titrate to perfusion and stop if there are signs of fluid overload. Where intensive care isn't available and the child isn't hypotensive, no bolus is suggested.

reference.label: Weiss SL, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign international guidelines for septic shock and sepsis-associated organ dysfunction in children. Intensive Care Med 2020;46(Suppl 1):10-67

questions.stem: A woman has a postpartum haemorrhage 1 hour after delivery. When should tranexamic acid be given?
options: Only if bleeding continues after 24 hours
1 g IV as soon as possible, within 3 hours of birth
questions.explanation: In WOMAN, TXA cut deaths from bleeding, especially when given within 3 hours of birth. Give 1 g IV, and a second 1 g if bleeding continues after 30 minutes.

reference.label: WOMAN Trial Collaborators. Effect of early tranexamic acid administration on mortality, hysterectomy, and other morbidities in women with post-partum haemorrhage (WOMAN). Lancet 2017;389:2105-2116

questions.stem: A farmer drank paraquat 1 hour ago and is alert. Which gut decontamination step is advised?
questions.explanation: Activated charcoal or Fuller's earth is given to limit absorption. Gastric lavage shouldn't be done. Haemodialysis or haemoperfusion is unlikely to change the course.

reference.label: Gawarammana IB, Buckley NA. Medical management of paraquat ingestion. Br J Clin Pharmacol 2011;72:745-757

questions.stem: You are placing an internal jugular central line. What is recommended for finding the vein and puncturing it?
options: A static ultrasound check, then a blind puncture
questions.explanation: Real-time ultrasound guidance is recommended for IJV cannulation. It cuts failed attempts and arterial puncture.

reference.label: American Society of Anesthesiologists Task Force on Central Venous Access. Practice guidelines for central venous access 2020. Anesthesiology 2020;132:8-43

questions.stem: You do a passive leg raise in a hypotensive patient while measuring cardiac output. Which change predicts fluid responsiveness?
options: A rise in CVP of 2 mmHg
A fall in heart rate of 5 bpm
A rise in cardiac output of 10% or more
questions.explanation: A PLR-induced rise in cardiac output of at least 10% reliably predicts fluid responsiveness (AUROC 0.95). Blood pressure alone is a much weaker guide. Measure CO (for example VTI), not BP.

reference.label: Monnet X, Marik P, Teboul JL. Passive leg raising for predicting fluid responsiveness: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Intensive Care Med 2016;42:1935-1947

questions.stem: A hypoxaemic patient (SpO₂ 90% on a face mask) needs emergency intubation in the ICU. Which preoxygenation method lowered hypoxaemia during intubation in the PREOXI trial?
questions.explanation: NIV preoxygenation halved hypoxaemia (SpO₂ < 85%) during intubation compared with an oxygen mask: 9.1% vs 18.5%.

reference.label: Gibbs KW, et al. Noninvasive ventilation for preoxygenation during emergency intubation (PREOXI). N Engl J Med 2024;390:2165-2177

questions.stem: You prescribe CRRT for AKI in septic shock. Which delivered effluent dose is recommended?
questions.explanation: KDIGO recommends a delivered dose of 20–25 mL/kg/h. In the RENAL trial, 40 mL/kg/h didn't lower 90-day mortality compared with 25 mL/kg/h. Prescribe a little more to allow for downtime.

reference.label: RENAL Replacement Therapy Study Investigators. Intensity of continuous renal-replacement therapy in critically ill patients. N Engl J Med 2009;361:1627-1638

questions.stem: A young man is on day 4 of dengue. His fever is settling. Which finding is a warning sign that means admission and close monitoring?
options: Platelets of 140 ×10⁹/L with a stable haematocrit
questions.explanation: WHO warning signs are abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, fluid accumulation, mucosal bleeding, lethargy or restlessness, liver enlargement more than 2 cm, and a rising haematocrit with a rapidly falling platelet count. The critical phase often starts as the fever settles.

reference.label: WHO. Dengue: guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, prevention and control. Geneva: WHO; 2009

questions.stem: A patient on warfarin has an intracerebral haemorrhage. INR is 3.4. What is the best reversal?
questions.explanation: 4F-PCC corrects the INR faster than FFP and with less volume. Give IV vitamin K with it so the INR doesn't rebound.

reference.label: Greenberg SM, et al. 2022 Guideline for the management of patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2022;53:e282-e361

questions.stem: Lung ultrasound in a breathless patient shows many B-lines in both lungs, in several zones on each side. What does this pattern indicate?
options: Interstitial syndrome, for example pulmonary oedema
questions.explanation: Multiple diffuse bilateral B-lines mean interstitial syndrome, most often cardiogenic oedema or ARDS. In pneumothorax, B-lines and lung sliding are absent.

reference.label: Volpicelli G, et al. International evidence-based recommendations for point-of-care lung ultrasound. Intensive Care Med 2012;38:577-591

questions.stem: A patient with aneurysmal SAH has had the aneurysm secured. Which drug, given for 21 days, improves neurological outcome?
questions.explanation: Oral nimodipine 60 mg every 4 hours for 21 days improves outcome in aSAH. Prophylactic hypervolaemia isn't recommended.

reference.label: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the management of patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. Stroke 2023

questions.stem: A monitored patient with a long QT goes into polymorphic VT that looks like torsades de pointes. It is self-terminating and they still have a pulse. What is the best first drug?
questions.explanation: IV magnesium is the treatment for torsades with a long QT. Amiodarone can prolong the QT further.

reference.label: Panchal AR, et al. Part 3: Adult basic and advanced life support: 2020 AHA guidelines. Circulation 2020

questions.stem: A ventilated patient with severe asthma becomes hypotensive. Expiratory flow doesn't return to zero before the next breath. What is the best immediate step?
options: Raise the respiratory rate to clear CO₂
Briefly disconnect from the ventilator, then reduce the rate and tidal volume to lengthen expiratory time
Give a fluid bolus and leave the settings alone
questions.explanation: This is dynamic hyperinflation (auto-PEEP). Let the patient exhale, then reduce minute ventilation and accept permissive hypercapnia.

reference.label: Leatherman J. Mechanical ventilation for severe asthma. Chest 2015

questions.stem: During apnoea testing for brain death, the patient is apnoeic. Which arterial result completes a positive test?
options: PaCO₂ ≥ 60 mmHg and ≥ 20 mmHg above baseline, with pH ≤ 7.30
questions.explanation: Those are the thresholds in the 2023 brain death consensus guideline. Follow the THOA/state protocol for the legal steps in India.

reference.label: Greer DM, et al. Pediatric and adult brain death/death by neurologic criteria consensus guideline. Neurology 2023

questions.stem: A ventilated ICU patient is started on an insulin infusion. Which glucose target is supported by the NICE-SUGAR trial?
options: A conventional target of about 140–180 mg/dL (insulin if glucose exceeds 180)
Keep glucose below 110 mg/dL in every ICU patient
questions.explanation: Tight control to 81–108 mg/dL increased 90-day mortality compared with a conventional target (insulin if glucose exceeds 180, then 144–180 mg/dL).

reference.label: NICE-SUGAR Study Investigators. Intensive versus conventional glucose control in critically ill patients. N Engl J Med 2009

questions.stem: A patient with ARDS is ventilated at 6 mL/kg predicted body weight. The plateau pressure is 34 cmH₂O. What's the best adjustment?
options: Accept this plateau and raise the tidal volume to 10 mL/kg
Lower the tidal volume (toward 4 mL/kg PBW) to keep plateau pressure ≤ 30 cmH₂O
Raise PEEP until the plateau is 40 cmH₂O
questions.explanation: ARDSNet lung-protective ventilation targets 6 mL/kg PBW (range 4–8) and keeps plateau pressure ≤ 30 cmH₂O.

reference.label: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome Network. Ventilation with lower tidal volumes for acute lung injury and the acute respiratory distress syndrome. N Engl J Med 2000

questions.stem: A patient with decompensated cirrhosis has AKI. Diuretics and nephrotoxins have been stopped, and albumin 1 g/kg has been given for 2 days, but creatinine is still rising. There is no shock. What's the usual next drug for HRS-AKI, and which adverse effect should you watch for?
options: Terlipressin (with albumin); watch for respiratory failure
questions.explanation: After a volume challenge, terlipressin plus albumin is used for HRS-AKI. In CONFIRM, respiratory failure was more common with terlipressin.

reference.label: Wong F, et al. Terlipressin plus albumin for the treatment of type 1 hepatorenal syndrome (CONFIRM). N Engl J Med 2021

questions.stem: A severely malnourished patient is starting enteral nutrition. Which electrolyte change is the hallmark of refeeding syndrome, and how should you start calories?
options: Hypernatraemia; start at 35 kcal/kg from day 1
Hypophosphataemia; start low, about 10–20 kcal/kg in the first 24 hours
Hypercalcaemia; start parenteral nutrition at full target
questions.explanation: Refeeding drives phosphate (and potassium and magnesium) intracellularly. ASPEN advises starting at 10–20 kcal/kg for the first 24 hours in high-risk patients, with close electrolyte replacement.

reference.label: da Silva JSV, et al. ASPEN consensus recommendations for refeeding syndrome. Nutr Clin Pract 2020

questions.stem: You are treating thyroid storm. What's the correct order of antithyroid drugs and iodine?
options: Give iodine first, then PTU 30 minutes later
Start a thionamide (PTU or methimazole) first, then give iodine at least 1 hour later
questions.explanation: Block hormone synthesis first, then give iodine, so iodine is not used as substrate for more hormone. Also give a beta-blocker and a steroid.

reference.label: Ross DS, et al. 2016 American Thyroid Association guidelines for diagnosis and management of hyperthyroidism and other causes of thyrotoxicosis. Thyroid 2016

questions.stem: You are inserting a central line. Which skin antiseptic is recommended to reduce CLABSI?
questions.explanation: SHEA 2022 recommends alcoholic chlorhexidine > 0.5% for CVC skin preparation (then allow it to dry).

reference.label: Buetti N, et al. Strategies to prevent central line-associated bloodstream infections in acute-care hospitals: 2022 update. Infect Control Hosp Epidemiol 2022

questions.stem: A 74-year-old with septic shock is on noradrenaline. Which initial MAP range does SSC 2026 suggest for patients aged 65 or older?
questions.explanation: For adults aged 65 or older, SSC 2026 suggests an initial MAP of 60–65 mmHg over higher ranges (conditional, low certainty). For other adults, an initial target of 65 mmHg is recommended.

reference.label: Prescott HC, et al. Executive summary: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026. Crit Care Med 2026

questions.stem: A patient with methanol poisoning is already on fomepizole. They develop new visual loss. The pH is 7.28. What's the best next step?
options: Observe, because fomepizole is already running
Give folinic acid only and repeat the pH in 6 hours
Give a bicarbonate bolus and discharge to the ward
questions.explanation: EXTRIP recommends extracorporeal treatment for new visual loss (also coma, seizures, pH ≤ 7.15, a persistent high anion gap, or a high methanol level). Intermittent haemodialysis is preferred.

reference.label: Roberts DM, et al. Recommendations for the role of extracorporeal treatments in acute methanol poisoning (EXTRIP). Crit Care Med 2015

questions.stem: A patient with a COPD exacerbation is still acidotic after nebulisers and steroids. The ABG is pH 7.28, PaCO₂ 68 mmHg, PaO₂ 62 mmHg on 28% oxygen. They are alert and protecting their airway. What's the best next step?
options: Start NIV (BiPAP) for hypercapnic respiratory failure
Give a 28% Venturi mask only and repeat the ABG tomorrow
questions.explanation: After medical therapy, pH < 7.35 with PaCO₂ > 45 mmHg is the usual trigger for NIV in COPD. ERS/ATS gives this a strong recommendation if the airway is protected.

reference.label: Rochwerg B, et al. Official ERS/ATS clinical practice guidelines: noninvasive ventilation for acute respiratory failure. Eur Respir J 2017

questions.stem: A patient with new atrial fibrillation has a BP of 78/50, cold skin and a lactate of 4.2 mmol/L. There is no known pre-excitation. What's the best immediate treatment?
questions.explanation: Haemodynamically unstable AF needs immediate synchronised cardioversion, not rate-control drugs first.

reference.label: Van Gelder IC, et al. 2024 ESC Guidelines for the management of atrial fibrillation. Eur Heart J 2024

questions.stem: A patient expected to stay ventilated for at least 48 h has no GI bleeding. What did the REVISE trial show for IV pantoprazole 40 mg daily compared with placebo?
options: Fewer clinically important upper GI bleeds (about 1% vs 3.5%), with no clear change in mortality
questions.explanation: Pantoprazole cut clinically important upper GI bleeding without a clear difference in 90-day mortality or pneumonia.

reference.label: Cook D, et al. Stress ulcer prophylaxis during invasive mechanical ventilation (REVISE). N Engl J Med 2024

questions.stem: A patient with DKA has K⁺ 3.0 mmol/L and is about to start insulin. There is no other emergency. What's the best next step?
options: Start insulin now and replace potassium later
Hold insulin and replace potassium first, until K⁺ is at least 3.3 mmol/L
Give 50 mL of 8.4% sodium bicarbonate, then start insulin
Give a 50% dextrose bolus, then start insulin
questions.explanation: Starting insulin when K⁺ is below 3.3 mmol/L can cause dangerous hypokalaemia. Replace potassium first, then start insulin.

reference.label: Umpierrez GE, et al. Hyperglycemic crises in adults with diabetes: a consensus report. Diabetes Care 2024

questions.stem: A man's baseline creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL. After a day in ICU it is 2.2 mg/dL, and urine output has been 0.4 mL/kg/h for 14 hours. What is the KDIGO AKI stage?
questions.explanation: KDIGO stage 2 is a 2.0–2.9-fold rise in creatinine or urine output below 0.5 mL/kg/h for 12 hours or more. Stage 3 needs a 3-fold rise, creatinine ≥ 4.0 mg/dL, RRT, or more severe oliguria.

reference.label: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury. Kidney Int Suppl 2012

questions.stem: A woman with septic shock has been resuscitated. She is not bleeding and has no acute coronary syndrome. Her Hb is 7.4 g/dL. Best transfusion plan?
options: Transfuse to a target of 9–10 g/dL
Hold blood; transfuse at Hb < 7, target 7–9
Give 2 units now because she is on noradrenaline
questions.explanation: TRISS and SSC support a restrictive threshold of 7 g/dL in septic shock without active bleeding or acute coronary syndrome.

reference.label: Holst LB, et al. Lower versus higher hemoglobin threshold for transfusion in septic shock (TRISS). N Engl J Med 2014; SSC 2026

questions.stem: A comatose adult has ROSC after cardiac arrest. There is no separate indication for hypothermia to 33°C. What should you do about temperature?
options: Allow fever up to 39°C if the patient is otherwise stable
Prevent fever, keeping temperature at 37.5°C or below
Warm to 38.5°C to improve neurological recovery
questions.explanation: TTM2 and current ILCOR, ERC and AHA guidance favour preventing fever over routine cooling to 33°C after ROSC.

reference.label: Dankiewicz J, et al. Hypothermia versus normothermia after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (TTM2). N Engl J Med 2021

questions.stem: A patient develops anaphylaxis (wheeze, low BP, urticaria) after a drug. What is the first-line treatment?
options: IV adrenaline 1 mg, as in cardiac arrest
IM adrenaline 0.5 mg (1:1000) into the anterolateral mid-thigh
IV hydrocortisone 200 mg as the first drug
Subcutaneous adrenaline 0.3 mg into the arm
questions.explanation: First-line treatment is IM adrenaline 0.5 mg of 1:1000 in the anterolateral mid-thigh. IV adrenaline is reserved for peri-arrest or a titrated infusion by experienced staff. Steroids are only adjuncts.

reference.label: Resuscitation Council UK. Emergency treatment of anaphylaxis: guidelines 2021

questions.stem: A patient with a confirmed PE has BP 80/50 that has stayed low for 20 minutes and a dilated RV on echo. There's no contraindication to bleeding. What's the best next step?
questions.explanation: High-risk (haemodynamically unstable) PE needs reperfusion, and systemic thrombolysis is first-line.

reference.label: ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of acute pulmonary embolism. Eur Heart J 2019

questions.stem: A man with Guillain-Barré syndrome has worsening weakness. Which finding most strongly points to elective intubation?
questions.explanation: The "20/30/40" rule is FVC below 20 mL/kg, MIP weaker than −30 cmH₂O and MEP below 40 cmH₂O. SpO₂ and PaCO₂ worsen late.

reference.label: Lawn ND, et al. Anticipating mechanical ventilation in Guillain-Barré syndrome. Arch Neurol 2001

questions.stem: A woman took paracetamol tablets repeatedly over about 12 hours (a staggered overdose). She feels well, and her ALT is normal. What's the right approach?
options: Plot the level on the nomogram and treat only if it's above the line
Start IV acetylcysteine without waiting for the level
Repeat the level in 4 hours, then decide
questions.explanation: The nomogram can't be read after a staggered overdose or when the time is unknown, so start acetylcysteine.

reference.label: MHRA Drug Safety Update. Treating paracetamol overdose with intravenous acetylcysteine: new guidance. 2012

questions.stem: A trauma patient arrives 1 hour after injury with bleeding and haemorrhagic shock. What does the evidence say about tranexamic acid?
options: Give 1 g IV over 10 minutes within 3 hours, then 1 g over 8 hours
Avoid it because of clot risk
Give it only if fibrinogen is low
questions.explanation: CRASH-2 showed lower mortality when TXA was given early. Starting it after 3 hours didn't help and may cause harm.

reference.label: CRASH-2 trial collaborators. Effects of tranexamic acid on death, vascular occlusive events, and transfusion in trauma patients. Lancet 2010

questions.stem: On day 7 of UFH, a patient's platelets fall from 250 to 95 ×10⁹/L and a new DVT appears. The 4Ts score is high. What's the best step?
options: Stop all heparin and start a non-heparin anticoagulant (e.g. argatroban or fondaparinux)
Stop heparin and give no anticoagulant
questions.explanation: Suspected HIT with thrombosis needs every form of heparin stopped, LMWH included, and a non-heparin anticoagulant started. Platelets are avoided.

reference.label: Cuker A, et al. American Society of Hematology 2018 guidelines for HIT. Blood Adv 2018

questions.stem: A woman at 34 weeks has an eclamptic seizure. Best first drug?
options: Magnesium sulphate 4 g IV over 15-20 min
questions.explanation: Magnesium is first-line for eclampsia (4 g IV load, then 1 g/h for 24 h) and beats diazepam and phenytoin at preventing further seizures.

reference.label: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222: Gestational hypertension and preeclampsia. Obstet Gynecol 2020; Magpie Trial, Lancet 2002

questions.stem: Chronic hyponatraemia, Na+ 112, in a malnourished man with alcohol use disorder and no severe symptoms. Maximum safe rise in Na+ in the first 24 h?
questions.explanation: High osmotic-demyelination risk (alcohol, malnutrition, hypokalaemia): aim for 4-8 and never exceed 8 mmol/L in 24 h; the limit is 10 for others.

reference.label: Verbalis JG et al. Diagnosis, evaluation, and treatment of hyponatremia: expert panel recommendations. Am J Med 2013

questions.stem: Seizures continue after two adequate doses of lorazepam. Correct next step?
questions.explanation: Second-line drugs must be given at full loading dose. In ESETT, levetiracetam 60 mg/kg, valproate 40 mg/kg and fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg each stopped seizures in about half of patients.

reference.label: Kapur J et al. Randomized trial of three anticonvulsant medications for status epilepticus (ESETT). N Engl J Med 2019

questions.stem: Cirrhosis with a variceal bleed, stable after resuscitation (Hb 7.8 g/dL, HR 102, BP 108/70). Best transfusion plan?
options: Hold blood; transfuse at Hb ≤ 7, target 7-8
questions.explanation: Restrictive transfusion: over-transfusion raises portal pressure and rebleeding. FFP isn't used to correct INR in cirrhosis.

reference.label: de Franchis R et al. Baveno VII: Renewing consensus in portal hypertension. J Hepatol 2022

questions.stem: A ventilated patient is CAM-ICU positive but calm and not distressed. Best approach?
options: Find and treat causes, ABCDEF bundle, re-screen every shift
questions.explanation: Haloperidol and ziprasidone did not shorten delirium (MIND-USA) and PADIS 2025 does not recommend routine antipsychotics; benzodiazepines and restraints worsen it.

reference.label: PADIS 2025 guideline update. Crit Care Med 2025; Girard TD et al. MIND-USA, N Engl J Med 2018

questions.stem: A 45-year-old with septic shock from aspiration pneumonia also has a traumatic brain injury from a fall. Which resuscitation fluid does SSC 2026 suggest?
questions.explanation: SSC 2026 suggests balanced crystalloids over saline in sepsis, but with a remark to use 0.9% saline when sepsis coexists with traumatic brain injury; starches are recommended against.

reference.label: Prescott HC, et al. Executive summary: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026. Crit Care Med. 2026 (statement 44 and remark)

questions.stem: A farmer with fever, an eschar, hypotension and PaO2/FiO2 of 180 is diagnosed with severe scrub typhus. Best antimicrobial regimen?
options: IV doxycycline plus IV azithromycin for 7 days
questions.explanation: In INTREST, combination IV doxycycline plus azithromycin reduced the composite of death, persistent complications or fever at day 7 compared with either drug alone; beta-lactams have no activity against Orientia.

reference.label: Varghese GM, et al. Intravenous doxycycline, azithromycin, or both for severe scrub typhus (INTREST). N Engl J Med. 2023;388(9):792-803

questions.stem: You perform a 20-minute whole blood clotting test (20WBCT) after a suspected viper bite. Which detail is essential for a valid result?
options: Use a new, clean, dry glass tube left undisturbed for 20 minutes
Use a plastic tube kept on ice
questions.explanation: Glass activates clotting; plastic, washed or wet tubes and disturbing the sample give false results. Blood that is still liquid when tilted at 20 minutes means venom-induced coagulopathy and is an indication for ASV.

reference.label: Lamb T, et al. The 20-minute whole blood clotting test (20WBCT) for snakebite coagulopathy: systematic review and meta-analysis. PLoS Negl Trop Dis. 2021;15(8):e0009657

questions.stem: A ventilated ARDS patient has PaO2/FiO2 of 110 on FiO2 0.7 and PEEP 12 despite lung-protective ventilation for 12 hours. Next best step?
options: Increase tidal volume to 8-10 mL/kg PBW
Prone positioning for at least 16 hours per session
Inhaled nitric oxide as a mortality-reducing therapy
questions.explanation: PROSEVA showed lower mortality with early prone positioning (≥16 h sessions) when P/F is below 150 mmHg on FiO2 ≥0.6 and PEEP ≥5; HFOV and iNO have not improved survival.

reference.label: Guérin C, et al. Prone positioning in severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSEVA). N Engl J Med. 2013;368(23):2159-2168

questions.stem: In septic shock with lactic acidosis, which patient fits the Surviving Sepsis Campaign suggestion to give IV sodium bicarbonate?
options: Any patient with lactate above 4 mmol/L, to improve vasopressor response
questions.explanation: SSC suggests against bicarbonate for hypoperfusion-related lactic acidaemia, except in severe acidaemia (pH ≤7.2) with AKI stage 2-3. A Nov 2026 meta-analysis found fewer patients needed RRT with bicarbonate but no clear survival benefit.

reference.label: Prescott HC, Antonelli M, Alhazzani W, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026. Intensive Care Med. 2026;52(5):863-936

sets.title: Starter set: drawn from the module quizzes

questions.stem: Which hour-1 bundle element carries a STRONG recommendation in SSC 2026?
options: Antibiotics within 1 h in septic shock
questions.explanation: Antibiotics immediately (ideally within 1 h) in septic shock or probable sepsis is strong; 'at least 30 mL/kg' remains conditional with low-certainty evidence, and SSC 2026 suggests crystalloid alone over added albumin.

reference.label: Prescott HC, Antonelli M, Alhazzani W, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026. Intensive Care Med. 2026;52(5):863-936. Co-published in Crit Care Med. 2026 (doi:10.1097/CCM.0000000000007075)

questions.explanation: Membrane stabilisation first.

reference.label: UK Kidney Association. Clinical practice guideline: Treatment of acute hyperkalaemia in adults (October…
